rationale: Systematic review compares endogenous lipid markers in fibromyalgia and chronic widespread pain; no sage intervention or Parkinson food comparison.
The Parkinson mouse model tests a pharmacological AC1 inhibitor on behavioral hyperalgesia. Sage is the publisher name and no fresh plant exposure was given.
The cross-sectional iRBD comparison analyzes handwriting, not a pain intervention. SAGE is the publisher; no fresh herb exposure was tested.
Pediatric epilepsy neuromodulation review notes chronic pain as prior stimulation context and painful stimulation effects; no sage treatment or pain outcome attributable to food.
Older men's Parkinson study discusses visual hallucinations in background and registry-derived psychotic disorders; no dried fig exposure or separate food analysis.
One of three described V15A Parkinson participants has a positive hallucination entry. No visual frequency scale, dried fig or dietary comparison is reported.
Review mentions hallucinations as a limitation of chronic levodopa therapy, with imaging focus; no dried fig or visual-hallucination food comparison.
Retrospective advanced Parkinson infusion cohorts report visual hallucinations including 17.54% subcutaneous and 28.57% intestinal group; no fig exposure, and groups differ clinically.
The systematic review evaluates molecular imaging in patients with Parkinson-associated variants. Fig denotes figures; no dried fig intake or ingredient-specific hallucination frequency is analyzed.
NILS observational Parkinson cohort evaluates drooling prevalence and progression; fig denotes figures and no fruit intervention is reported.
The review separates drug and injection interventions for Parkinson sialorrhea from its other sections. No raw fig or fig-specific drooling comparison.
A handwriting and dysgraphia discussion with a reference to a dystonia case does not report fresh sage treatment or a dystonia severity endpoint.
Pediatric epilepsy neuromodulation review lists dystonic posturing as stimulation-related motor adverse effect; not Parkinson dystonia or fresh sage exposure.
The qualitative Parkinson synthesis discusses off-period mobility and stiffness as restrictions on balance, without ground-sage exposure or a rigidity comparison.
Drooling cohort describes assessments and chronology; pain appears in a pain-scale author disclosure, without a pain outcome or dried date exposure.
Combined pain and sensory-disturbance entries are negative for three genotyped Parkinson participants. Dried dates were not investigated.
Fibromyalgia and chronic widespread pain studies include pain-intensity measures in biomarker comparison; no dried date or Parkinson treatment.
PD imaging review names pain among nonmotor symptoms; date is chronological wording, not date fruit or pain outcome following consumption.
Pain is mentioned as a separate use of focal lesioning and as a medication effect elsewhere. The review provides no dried-date pain intervention or intake data.
The Parkinson mouse experiments measure mechanical allodynia and hyperalgesia during AC1 perturbation. No dried-date intake or date-specific outcome.
Infusion-site pain described as adverse effect in subcutaneous levodopa pump recipients; no date-fruit exposure or food comparison.
The apomorphine-centered expert review mentions abdominal pain as an adverse event with intestinal levodopa infusion. No dried-date intervention or comparative pain outcome.
Noninvasive vagal stimulation in epilepsy review reports ear pain among adverse effects; no dried date or Parkinson food intervention.
Introduction names resting tremor as a diagnostic feature; study outcomes are affective disorder, psychosis and dementia, with no raw fig exposure.
Resting tremor is recorded in two of three described V15A cases. The study assays lipid binding and provides no raw fig intake or comparison.
Review identifies rest tremor as a diagnostic Parkinson feature; no raw fig comparison or tremor response to food.
The clinical review describes Parkinson resting tremor and differentiates it from essential tremor. No raw fig exposure or intake-linked tremor measurement.
Rest tremor is a Parkinson feature in the molecular-imaging review, with studies of genetic groups. No raw fig exposure or dose-linked tremor severity comparison.
The expert document discusses tremor as a clinical context for Parkinson device selection. No raw fig intervention or fig-linked resting tremor estimate.
NILS methods list mood/apathy as one domain of the NMSS in a drooling cohort; no isolated apathy result or dried date exposure.
The Parkinson crossover compares citalopram and placebo on effort and reward, and includes baseline apathy measures. No dried dates or date-versus-control apathy estimate.
Clinical account states apathy following dopamine-agonist withdrawal limited discontinuation; no dried date exposure or food comparison.
The review discusses serotonin transporter binding and apathy separately from its genetic imaging synthesis. No dried date intake or date-linked apathy comparison.
The apomorphine review discusses apathy in advanced Parkinson disease and drug management. No dried date intervention or date-linked apathy estimate.
The study synthesis records carers' experiences of repeat falls in Parkinson disease. SAGE is the publisher, and no ground sage exposure or intake comparison was reported.
Gait variability review describes studies relating eGVI to Parkinson fall frequency; no ground sage exposure.
Review identifies severe fatigue as a fibromyalgia symptom while examining endogenous pain biomarkers; no fresh sage fatigue comparison.
The clinical study identifies fatigue among depression questionnaire items and controls task fatigue, with citalopram and placebo sessions and no fresh sage.
The Parkinson mobility synthesis discusses physical burdens and fatigue around off-periods without fresh-sage exposure or a fatigue severity comparison.
The cross-sectional sleep disorder study reports handwriting markers and cognitive or motor characteristics, without a fatigue intervention or fresh sage exposure.
Review discusses fatigue sensitivity of gait variability in multiple sclerosis; no fresh sage or isolated fatigue intervention.
The citalopram and placebo experiment examines motivated decision-making and baseline apathy measures in Parkinson disease. No ground sage exposure or sage-specific apathy estimate.
Review discusses factors that shorten stride and variability in Parkinson or older people; no ground sage consumption or comparative effect.

CIIS 2023 member O16 examines migraine pain perception; another member P66 evaluates spinal-cord injury pain. Sage occurs as a publisher surname in a separate reference, not a plant exposure in either member.
CIIS member P66 examines pain variation in one spinal-cord injury patient during brain-machine interface control; no date-fruit intervention or Parkinson comparison within member.
Community men's Parkinson study uses administrative affective, psychotic and dementia outcomes; no specific apathy assessment or date-fruit exposure found.
Time maintaining balance on a rotating drum served as a motor assay in mice. It gives no clinical fall frequency or ground sage exposure; Sage is the publisher.
CIIS member P65 compares tactile feedback in seven exoskeleton users and reports fatigue p=0.65; no sage intervention and no Parkinson cohort specified.
